whatThePageStates: The page describes the IP reputation category of AWS Managed Rules for AWS WAF and names the rule groups AWS publishes in that category. It has two H2 sections, one per rule group: 'Amazon IP reputation list managed rule group' (VendorName AWS, Name AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList, WCU 25) and 'Anonymous IP list managed rule group' (VendorName AWS, Name AWSManagedRulesAnonymousIpList, WCU 50). Each section carries a two-column table (Rule name | Description and label) listing the individual rules inside that group, with each rule's default action and its label string: three rules for the Amazon IP reputation list, two for the Anonymous IP list. The only explicit negative on the page is a category-wide statement that these rule groups do not provide versioning or SNS update notifications, plus an in-description exclusion that the HostingProviderIPList does not include AWS IP addresses. There is no support matrix, no Yes/No column, no Region column, and no per-plan column anywhere on the page.

features.featureName: IP reputation rule groups (AWS Managed Rules for AWS WAF)
features.collapse: The page's rows are individual rules, not rule groups. Five rule rows appear across two tables: three rows (AWSManagedIPReputationList, AWSManagedReconnaissanceList, AWSManagedIPDDoSList) all belong to the single rule group AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList, and two rows (AnonymousIPList, HostingProviderIPList) both belong to the single rule group AWSManagedRulesAnonymousIpList. 3+2=5 rows collapse to 2 distinct managed rule groups. The rule group is the unit AWS names with VendorName/Name/WCU and the unit a customer actually adds to a web ACL, so it is the axis value; the rule rows are its contents.
features.statuses: No status column exists. 5 rule rows, all present-means-offered; 3+2=5. There is no Yes/No/Partial split to read, because the page is an enumeration, not a matrix. The nearest thing to a per-row status is the default 'Rule action' string: 4 Block, 1 Count (AWSManagedIPDDoSList is Count); 4+1=5. That is the rule's default action inside the group, NOT a support status, and must not be mapped onto Yes/No/Partial. Not-supported is never stated for any rule group. The two explicit negatives on the page are about attributes, not coverage: 'The rule groups in this category don't provide versioning or SNS update notifications' (a category-wide feature caveat covering both groups) and 'The IP list does not include AWS IP addresses' (a content exclusion inside the HostingProviderIPList description). Neither is a No against an enumerated axis value.
features.scope: None. There is no second dimension. The page states no Region, partition, plan, tier, or protected-resource-type scoping for either rule group. WCU (25, 50) and VendorName are per-group metadata, not a scope axis, and the label strings are identifiers, not scopes.
features.reasoning: The page's own framing is 'Choose one or more of these rule groups', so the thing being enumerated is the set of AWS-published managed rule groups in the IP reputation category — a catalogue the service publishes about itself, which is exactly managedRuleGroup. The unit of claim is the rule group, because that is what AWS names (VendorName/Name), prices in WCU, and what a customer references in a web ACL. The individual rules are sub-items of a group and are described, not offered, independently.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Introducing a new console experience for AWS WAF' banner at the top. The Note box about source IP addresses behind proxies and load balancers. The two identical Note boxes of boilerplate ('The information that we publish for the rules in the AWS Managed Rules rule groups...contact the AWS Support Center') — repeated once per section, so a naive count double-counts them. Per-group metadata lines (VendorName: AWS, Name: ..., WCU: 25 / WCU: 50) — WCU is a capacity number, not a count of anything covered. The two table header rows and two markdown separator rows ('| Rule name | Description and label |' and '| --- | --- |'), which would inflate a row count from 5 to 9. Label strings such as awswaf:managed:aws:amazon-ip-list:AWSManagedIPReputationList, which are identifiers, not axis values. The 'Rule action: Block/Count' fragments, which are default actions, not statuses. Outbound links (Working with the console, Bot Control rule group, Web request labeling, Label metrics and dimensions, the MadPot news article, AWS Support Center). The entire 'See also' section, which is the optional AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit boilerplate and carries no coverage claim.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no Region list, no Region table, and no partition. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing enumerable. The page concerns exactly one service, AWS WAF, and does not enumerate services; other AWS services are mentioned only in passing (CloudWatch for label metrics, Amazon Support). It is not a service-coverage page. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. The page never lists the protected resource types a web ACL can be associated with (no CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, App Runner, Cognito, Verified Access enumeration). The only dimension this page actually supplies is a catalogue one: which managed rule groups exist in the IP reputation category (2), and which rules sit inside them (5).
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting the 5 rule rows as 5 rule groups — the tables are the most table-like thing on the page, so a row-harvesting parser reports 5 managed rule groups when AWS offers 2 in this category. Runners-up: (1) counting markdown table lines rather than data rows, giving 9 (5 data + 2 headers + 2 separators) or 7; (2) reading the 'Rule action' values as a support status split (4 Block / 1 Count) and emitting a tri-state Yes/No/Partial that the page never asserts; (3) treating 'don't provide versioning or SNS update notifications' as an explicit No against an axis value, when it is a category-wide attribute caveat with no axis behind it; (4) treating 'The IP list does not include AWS IP addresses' as a not-supported entry rather than a description of one rule's list contents; (5) harvesting the label strings or the VendorName/Name/WCU metadata as additional axis values; (6) counting the two repeated boilerplate Note boxes as content; (7) inventing a Region or resource-type figure from a page that is silent on both.
